generatedProse.concept-context: Psychology prizes imaginative reading. A study is not just a result to record: it is an interpretation you can open up. An imaginative reader asks what a finding could mean beyond the authors' own account, links it to a theory from another area, and considers a case the study never tested, while staying anchored in the method and the data. That is analysis with imagination, not invention.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students write about the same interpretation of a well-known study.

Tom reports the interpretation accurately: this is what the authors argue, and this is the evidence. The summary is correct and clear. But it stops there. Tom records what the study says and adds nothing, so the reader learns the finding but not what to make of it.

Amara examines the same interpretation closely, then opens it up. What else could this effect mean? Amara connects it to a theory from another module the authors never mention, and offers an original reading, still anchored in the sample and the method. The study becomes a starting point, not a closed result.

Both students understood the study. Only Amara read it imaginatively, making a connection of her own rather than only summarising.
generatedProse.summary: Imaginative analysis brings creativity to how you read psychology. You examine a study closely, then open it up: asking what a finding could mean, making original connections, and bringing in theory the authors never cited, while staying anchored in the method and the data. You can now tell an imaginative reading from a routine one and produce connections of your own. Across the course you have put creative methods to work: generating and organising ideas, thinking flexibly across approaches, and reading with imagination.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's reading more than a summary?

items.text: She connected the study to another theory and produced an original reading grounded in the method and data.
She reported the authors' argument more accurately.
She wrote at greater length about the study.
She quoted the authors' own conclusion.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara made an original connection, grounded in the evidence, which goes beyond summarising.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara added that Tom did not.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's reading went beyond summary because she made an original connection to another theory, anchored in the method and data. Accuracy, length or quotation do not.
